To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
PI‐9 expression is up‐regulated by activation of monocytes in vitro, and by EBV infection in vivo.
PI‐9 expression is up‐regulated in monocytes, not lymphocytes, following stimulation with several stimuli including LPS, and in lymphocytes and macrophage from patients with acute EBV infection.
PI‐9, an endogenous natural inhibitor of granzyme B, is up‐regulated in monocytes upon stimulation with bacterial or viral agents.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of PI-9, an intracellular serine protease inhibitor (serpin) expressed in lymphocytes, macrophages and dendritic cells.
the modulation of PI‐9 by stimulation and by infection.
a better understanding of the role of PI‐9 during infection, and the regulation of PI-9 in the immune system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PI‐9 expression is up‐regulated in monocytes upon activation, and that this is a rapid and reversible process.
PI‐9 expression is up‐regulated upon activation of monocytes, whereas lymphocyte expression is stable.
PI‐9 levels are increased in the presence of bacterial and viral infection, but not during bacterial infection in preterm infants.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PI‐9 expression is up‐regulated in monocytes upon activation, but not in lymphocytes, which may indicate a specific function in the inflammatory response.
PI‐9 expression is up‐regulated by stimulation of PBMCs, but not by infection with bacteria, or by EBV.
PI‐9 expression is regulated by the immune system in response to infection, and is up‐regulated by monocyte‐activating stimuli.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PI‐9 expression is regulated in a cell type‐specific manner by stimulation of monocytes and lymphocytes in vitro and in patients with viral infection.
PI‐9 expression is up‐regulated in monocytes by activation and infection.
PI‐9 can be rapidly up‐regulated in monocytes by stimulation, and is also induced in patients with EBV infection, but not bacterial infection.
